states.question: Does setting A to +1 increase Y enough to justify cost rho/2?
assumptions: Specified finite nominal and contamination SCM families
Known mechanism coefficients and Gaussian noise
Perfect interventions
Independent post-intervention samples
warnings: All intervention results are simulated, not real-world experimental verification.
Observational likelihood is identical across hypotheses; arrow orientation is unresolved before intervention.
Model probabilities are conditional on the candidate family, not proof of causal structure.
Shadow models challenge the nominal causal family. Their posterior mass measures risk relative to the specified alternatives.
A model-risk alert is not proof of a real-world negative treatment effect.
All mechanism coefficients and the finite shadow set are fixed, not estimated from these experiments.
states.interval_type: Finite contamination-family 95% posterior credible envelope; not a general confidence interval
states.risk_definition: Three-class classification with reject loss 0.10; operational claim guard is separate
